title: Tech Note: Introduction to 4D for OCI
author: Yvan Ayaay, Technical Support Engineer, 4D Inc.
featured_technology: Oracle Instant Client / Oracle Database Client installation

historical_commentary.text: This note introduces the 4D for OCI plug-in, which gave 4D 2004 applications native client connectivity to Oracle 8i/9i/10g servers via Oracle's Call Interface, and walks through installing the Oracle Client/Instant Client and configuring tnsnames.ora on both Windows and Mac OS X. The 4D for OCI plug-in has since been discontinued as a distinct product, and the manual Mac OS X installation steps shown (copying dylibs to /usr/lib, editing environment.plist) are tied to system conventions long superseded by later macOS security and library-loading changes, making the specific instructions obsolete even though the general concept of connecting 4D to Oracle via a client library remains a live requirement addressed through other means today.
related_updates: The 4D for OCI plug-in has been discontinued; direct Oracle connectivity is no longer offered as this dedicated plug-in
4D's SQL engine (from v11 SQL onward) and ODBC-based external database connections are the current paths for connecting 4D applications to Oracle and other external databases
macOS library installation and security conventions (e.g., dylib loading, SIP) have changed substantially since Mac OS X 10.3
